nodes.description: Private address state variable storing the beneficiary of the tokens after release.
Private bool state variable flag indicating whether the timelock has been initiated.
Private uint256 state variable holding the timestamp when token release becomes enabled.
TokenTimelock constructor that assigns the beneficiary address to _beneficiary.
initiateLock(uint256) sets _releaseTime and flips _lockInitiated; guarded by msg.sender == _beneficiary and releaseTime > block.timestamp.
View function returning the stored _beneficiary address.
View function returning the stored _releaseTime timestamp.
View function returning the _lockInitiated boolean flag.
View function returning whether block.timestamp is greater than or equal to _releaseTime.
View function returning the timelock contract's balance of a given ERC20 token.
increaseLock(uint256) increases _releaseTime; guarded by _lockInitiated, msg.sender == _beneficiary and newReleaseTime > _releaseTime.
release(IERC20) transfers the whole token balance to _beneficiary once block.timestamp >= _releaseTime; performs an external token transfer.
TwittelonInuTimelock constructor forwarding the beneficiary to the TokenTimelock base constructor.
msg.sender, attacker-controllable caller address used in access control checks in initiateLock and increaseLock.
block.timestamp, miner-influenceable time value used in lock initiation, unlock check and release check.
External ERC20 token transfer (token.safeTransfer) to _beneficiary inside release; state effect order and external call create a reentrancy surface.
Parameter releaseTime of initiateLock, caller-supplied unlock timestamp written into _releaseTime.
Parameter newReleaseTime of increaseLock, caller-supplied timestamp written into _releaseTime.
Parameter token of release, the ERC20 token instance whose balance is transferred.
Parameter token of holdings, the ERC20 token instance queried for balance.
Parameter beneficiary of the constructor, written into the _beneficiary state variable.
Local variable amount in release holding the contract's token balance before transfer.

edges.reason: initiateLock requires msg.sender == _beneficiary, so the untrusted caller governs whether the lock can be initiated.
increaseLock requires msg.sender == _beneficiary, making the untrusted caller the gate for modifying the release time.
initiateLock's require(releaseTime > block.timestamp) depends on the miner-influenceable block.timestamp for a lock condition.
unlocked() compares block.timestamp >= _releaseTime, an outcome influenced by timestamp manipulation.
release() requires block.timestamp >= _releaseTime, so the transfer is gated by the timestamp value.
unlocked() reads the _releaseTime state variable to compute the branch result.
release() reads _releaseTime in its require check before transferring tokens.
increaseLock compares newReleaseTime with the current _releaseTime and overwrites it.
release() requires the _lockInitiated flag to be true before executing the transfer.
increaseLock requires the _lockInitiated flag to be true.
initiateLock writes true into the _lockInitiated flag after validating inputs.
The caller-supplied releaseTime parameter is written into the _releaseTime state variable.
The releaseTime parameter flows into the timestamp requirement and the state assignment within initiateLock.
The newReleaseTime parameter overwrites the _releaseTime state variable in increaseLock.
The newReleaseTime parameter is validated and used within increaseLock.
The constructor parameter beneficiary is assigned to the _beneficiary state variable.
The beneficiary parameter is the direct input consumed by the constructor.
release() reads the _beneficiary state variable and uses it as the target of the external token transfer.
The _beneficiary address is the recipient argument of the unsafe external safeTransfer call.
release() invokes the external token transfer, handing control to the token contract before any accounting update.
The external token transfer can re-enter release()/the token logic while the contract still holds tokens, a classic reentrancy path.
The local amount (full token balance) is the value passed into the external safeTransfer call.
The token parameter of release is the ERC20 instance on which the unsafe external transfer is invoked.
The token parameter's balanceOf result is stored in the local amount variable.
The token parameter of holdings is queried via balanceOf to return the timelock holdings.

normalization_plan.reason: The releaseTime parameter has no independent semantic identity beyond its use inside initiateLock.
The newReleaseTime parameter exists only as input validated and stored by increaseLock.
The token parameter of release flows directly into the external safeTransfer call and defines that unsafe operation's target.
The token parameter of holdings is only used to query a balance within that view function.
The beneficiary parameter is the sole input of the constructor and is immediately stored in state.
The local amount is the value argument of the external safeTransfer call and carries no meaning outside it.
